payload.label: Workflow recipes: step-by-step playbooks any person's AI can follow, one file each in recipes/
payload.invoke_with_why: A listed workflow row runs on the workflow component (tool:run-a-workflow): every ask is a wake effect the engine runs, and each pass is kept for tools:read {workflow_run} | {fact} (run_steps). Its definition is read from the row the person keeps (workflow_recipes) in the database the run names: its switch's kept_in.database, the kept_in of the fact that chose it (the same field the asked-row starter hands every run it starts), or the run's own database, so this shared row names none; a run whose reader names no database runs the definition it carries, and with none fails naming kept_in. tool:run-workflow-definition (the JS walker) is retired once every behaviour it alone has runs here (L101).

input.sql: SELECT recipe, definition, kept_at::text AS kept_at FROM workflow_recipes WHERE (recipe = $1::text OR recipe = ANY(coalesce($2::text[], '{}'))) AND jsonb_typeof(definition) = 'object' ORDER BY recipe = $1::text DESC, recipe

payload.label: Choose which of my workflows fire for these parts of a seed
payload.job: Say which of all my workflows, and the Workshop's I have installed, fire for each part of something that arrived, from the conditions each workflow carries on its own row
payload.description: Every workflow is a candidate branch of the one tree. Takes parts: the parts of one seed, each an object of its typed fields (for example kinds, subjects, people, niches, own_words; the fields are whatever the conditions read). Is given the person's own workflow rows as values (own), read by the caller from wherever the person keeps them, beside every recipe this Workshop installs; it reaches no database; an id the person holds a row for always shadows the installed recipe of that id, whatever the row's conditions (a row with none is unconditioned), and shadow_ids names every id the person holds a row for, so the installed copy of each is left out. Each workflow's conditions are its fires_when (branches/fires-when.json): a list of { label, condition: { fields, tree }, made_by, state }, the same fields and tree tool:filter-rows-by-rules takes, evaluated by the same formulas engine over the parts. Answers chosen (one row per workflow, part and condition that kept it: workflow, part, condition, input, installed, score, rank, and kept_in for an own row kept in a store, or definition for one handed in with it; ranked within each part by specificity: score is the sum over the tags or rules the part met of log(workflows with a condition / workflows holding that tag), times the condition's measured weight, rank 1 best), named (how many conditions are unfinished: a rule the engine cannot evaluate, no rule at all, or a field a part does not carry, which choose nothing; how many workflows are unconditioned, with no condition On; how many conditions are broad, keeping more than half of the parts; how many parts are unmatched), within and the counts. This answer is what a workflow run holds and carries in every later envelope, so it stays small. With explain: true it also names them, to be fixed: unfinished, unconditioned (by id and label, to be judged by their words), broad (to be rewritten) and unmatched_parts, and each choice's label, made_by, from, matched and weight. Nothing is written; no workflow, branch or tag is named in the tool.

parts.description: The seed's parts, each an object of the typed fields the conditions read

operators.description: Comparisons and combinators as rows of data, as tool:filter-rows-by-rules takes them; left out for the built-in ones

shadow_ids.description: Every workflow id the person holds a row for: each installed copy of those ids is left out, whatever the row holds. Left out, none is shadowed.

within.description: The workflow ids of the runs this choice is made inside (the run itself and every run above it); none of them is chosen again, so no workflow starts itself through its own parts

own.description: The person's own workflow rows, read by the caller from wherever the person keeps them: each { id, value: { recipe?, title, fires_when, definition? } }. Left out, only the installed recipes are candidates. A chosen own row that carries its definition hands it on in chosen

installed.description: false leaves the installed recipes out, and every own row whose id an installed recipe holds: only the person's rows that exist nowhere else are candidates. Left out, true

explain.description: true also names what named counts (unfinished, unconditioned, broad, unmatched_parts) and why each choice was made (label, made_by, from, matched, weight), for whoever judges or fixes them. Left out, false: the answer a workflow run carries

over_installed.description: With installed false: workflow ids whose own rows are candidates even though an installed recipe holds the same id (the person's list of workflows moved to their own rows ahead of the rest)

payload.label: Write a copy of a repository into my files, for citations to be checked against
payload.job: Write the files of a repository, the dates of its commits and a stamp naming the commit into my own files under /source-copies/<root>/, so a check of what a finding cites can read them on any computer
payload.description: Takes a root name, the ref and head the copy was made from, a list of files ({path, text}, at most 64, each at most 4 MiB), the commit dates ({<full hash>: <ISO date>}), whether the list is every tracked file, and stored.files: the files already under /source-copies/<root>/ that the caller read from where the person keeps them (a file not handed in is not there). It reads and writes no store: it answers keep, each file { file, identity, base64, expected } in order (expected is the identity of the file as handed in, null when it was not there, so a store refuses a keep whose file moved): each file, then .commit-dates.json, and the stamp .source-copy.json last, under /source-copies/<root>/, so a copy whose stamp is old never claims a new head. A file handed in that already holds the bytes sent is left out of keep. The stamp holds ref, head, copied_at and files: the sorted paths the copy holds (the earlier stamp's files plus these, or exactly these when complete is true; also_held paths, written by earlier runs of the same head, are added). A big copy can be sent in several runs: with final false a run keeps only its files (no dates, no stamp) and answers final:false; the last run (final true, the default) keeps the dates and the stamp. A path with .., ., an empty part, a leading / or a backslash is refused and nothing is kept. The tool never reads a repository: the caller reads git and hands in the text.

root.description: The name of the copy folder under /source-copies/ (the root name a resolver lists)

ref.description: The ref the copy was made from

head.description: The commit the copy was made from

files.description: The files to write, at their repository paths

dates.description: Full commit hash to ISO date

complete.description: True when the files sent are every tracked file of the repository

final.description: False writes only the files, with no dates and no stamp; the last run of a head leaves it true (the default)

also_held.description: Paths written by earlier non-final runs of the same head, added to the stamp's files

stored.description: What this run reads of the person's own things, read by the caller from where the person keeps them and handed in: files: {name: text or {base64}, or null when not there} under /source-copies/<root>/, at least the earlier stamp .source-copy.json. What is not given is not there.

keep.description: The files the run made, in order, for the caller to keep where the person keeps them: { file, identity, base64, expected } (expected is the identity of the file as it was handed in, null when it was not there, so a store refuses the write when it moved). The run itself writes nothing.

payload.label: Run a read-only checklist gate on my files (runs on your computer)
payload.job: Before I am shown anything I made, list the required checks that apply to it and identify which answers are open, stale or failed, without changing my files
payload.description: Reads the person's checklist (stages, checks and routes), schema and piece from one folder they grant. It runs the existing checklist gate read-only: every required check that applies to the piece is listed with its current answer state, file identity and criterion pins. It accepts `gate`, `scope`, `audit` without `--hold`, read-only `checklist`, and `library-pending` for the next bounded source-assessment batch in the schema's current work context. It does not create a lock file, first-gate record or pin cache, and it cannot answer checks, run write-producing sweeps or hold files. The same generic checklist consumer still refuses empty or unknown scopes, reports stale answers and requires exact BLAKE3 file and definition pins. A separate write-grant tool handles commands that change the library. Nothing about a person's checklist or piece is known by this tool; the schema owns those details.

library.description: The folder the schema's files are relative to, put where {library} is in the command.

schema.description: The schema file on the person's computer (see the README for its keys), put where {schema} is in the command.

command.description: A read-only command: gate <piece> --stage ID[,ID] [--option ITEM]... [--at DELIVERY_STAGE]; scope <piece> [--lane NAME]; audit <piece> [--file PATH]...; checklist [--check|--problems]; or library-pending --limit 8 [--source-id ID]. Never include --hold or --write. Put the command after the schema in the command.

output_schema.description: { result, exit_code } from the existing gate consumer. For gate, result contains all_passed, the routed checks, stale or failed answers, and items not evaluated; scope lists item ids; audit lists offenders; checklist reports its generated comparison or problems. exit_code is 0 when the selected read passes, 1 when a gate is open or failed, and 2 for unreadable inputs. The private native run omits temporary answer command paths.

provenance.source: A pre-delivery gate over a person's own checklist where every answer is bound to the identity of the files it judged and every measuring tool's answer to the reviewed version of that tool

payload.label: Turn my written checklist into the checklist file the gate reads, and check that file (runs on your computer)
payload.job: Keep one written checklist of mine as the only source, generate the checklist document from it, tell me when the file on disk no longer matches my text, and find the mistakes a hand edit or a typo would make
payload.description: Reads a person's checklist text (one section per stage, one table row per check, notes that annotate a check, an optional file of rules whose wording is read from there and never copied) through the `checklist_source` part of the schema the person gives, which holds the regular expressions and constant fields that say how their text is laid out. `checklist` prints the document the text generates, `--check` says in words which checks differ from the file on disk, `--write` writes the file, and `--problems` checks the file on disk for repeated ids, a required flag that is not true or false, a route no reader can evaluate, a per-item check with no rule, an advisory stage that is not a delivery stage, a phase that names no check and counts that do not add up. It refuses a rule that has no row and a note that names no check. It knows no row kind, id shape or route tag.

library.description: The folder the schema's files are relative to, put where {library} is in the command.

schema.description: The schema file on the person's computer (its checklist_source part is described in the README), put where {schema} is in the command.

mode.description: One of: --check, --write, --problems, or leave it out to print the generated document. Put it where {mode} is in the command.

output_schema.description: --check and --problems print { all_passed, difference? | problems }; --write prints { written, checks, must }; with no mode the generated document. The exit status is 0 when everything passed, 1 when the file differs or has problems and 2 when the text or schema could not be read.

invoke.say: This runs on the person's own computer, from the root of the Workshop checkout. After the person edits their written checklist, run it with `--check`; if it says the file differs, run `--write`, then `--problems`, and tell the person what the text now generates and any problem found. Never edit the generated file by hand: the text is the source.

provenance.source: A checklist document generated from the person's own text by declared patterns, so there is one source and a check that the generated file has not drifted

payload.label: Record a checklist answer or run its checked steps (runs on your computer)
payload.job: Record a checklist answer or run a declared checker or gate, with the required folder change grant
payload.description: Uses the same checklist consumer as the read-only gate, but only after the person grants this tool permission to change one folder. It records the person's answer, imports a checker report under the reviewed checker pins, runs the schema's sweeps or gates, holds files only when requested, writes the checklist generated from the person's text, or records and removes source assessments in the existing applications DATA through `library-assess` and `library-remove`. Assessments require current source and work-context pins and preserve other contexts. The existing consumer still checks criteria definitions, BLAKE3 file pins, checker pins, scopes and stale rows; this tool adds no alternate answer or bypass.

library.description: The library folder inside the folder you grant for this run.

schema.description: The schema file inside the folder you grant for this run.

command.description: A write command: answer <piece> --check ID [--option ITEM] --answer pass|fail|n/a --evidence TEXT --by NAME; answers-from-report <piece> --json REPORT [--option ITEM]; sweep <piece> --previews FOLDER...; run-gates <piece> --lane-dir FOLDER; run-files <piece> --file PATH...; audit <piece> --hold; checklist --write; library-assess --json FILE; or library-remove --json FILE. The command is parsed as arguments, never shell text.

output_schema.description: { result, exit_code } from the existing checklist consumer, or { error, exit_code } when the command cannot run. An open or failed check remains failed; an answer is kept only under its own name and current file and criterion pins.

provenance.source: tools/workflows/do-work/checklist_gate.py: answer and checker operations share the same criterion, file and checker pins as the read-only gate

files.text:
# Sample checklist

**Delivery stages:** final = a loaf put on the shelf.

## S1. Bake
| S1.1 | Oven is preheated | all | Read the dial | habit | yes |
| S1.2 | Tray is clean | all | Look at it | habit | no |

## Notes

payload.label: Measure exact page citations across planned questions and answer engines
payload.job: Compare every planned page × question × answer engine cell against recorded answer observations, keeping exact page citations, unavailable answers and unasked cells distinct
payload.description: Builds the complete page × question × engine matrix from a plan and supplied observations. A citation counts only when its parsed HTTP(S) URL exactly matches the page URL, its supplied checked canonical URL, or an explicitly supplied verified redirect URL; a path prefix is never enough. Query strings remain significant and fragments are ignored. Original answers and citation links are preserved. Missing/not-run and unavailable cells stay unknown; only an observed answer with an explicit citations array can be cited or not cited. This tool measures supplied observations and does not query engines, establish who observed them, or prove why an engine cited a page.

questions.description: Questions this exact page answers; otherwise shared questions must be supplied.

canonical_url.description: Canonical address observed from the page; include only when checked.

verified_redirects.description: Redirect addresses actually observed while reaching this page.

questions.description: Shared questions planned for every page that does not provide its own questions.

provenance.source: tools/workflows/read-data/citation-coverage.mjs: complete planned matrix and exact checked page URL identities

payload.run_steps_why: Where a pass's result names its run, status, steps, waiting asks and workflow (the engine's src/tool_runs/tools/run_steps.rs): the engine keeps each finished pass as its run's summary, readable by tools:read {workflow_run} or {fact} (the event id of the fact that started it), so a run that made no waiting task can be read back (gap-a-workflow-run-without-tasks-cannot-be-read-back, Nov 21 2026).
payload.label: Run a workflow on the workflow engine, one step at a time
payload.job: Run one of my workflows from its definition: walk its steps with the answers held so far, start the tool each next step names, tell every other step as waiting, and run again when an answer is told
payload.description: The workflow engine as one WebAssembly component (tools/workflows/crates/workflow-component), run with no network, no secret and no door. A run is handed its definition by whatever started it, from where the person keeps their workflows: in its input, in its wake's switch input, or in the fact that woke it (definition and start_at). The engine walks it from the start with the answers held. A step that names a tool starts that tool as a wake effect, whose result (or why it failed) is told back as the fact workflow-step-answered, which runs this again with the answer. Any other step is told as the fact workflow-step-waiting with what it asks, whom, and told_as, the envelope its answer comes back in; the person's own wakes decide what it becomes (its wake a-step-is-waiting runs the definition its switch input carries, such as one that gives the step to its answerer as a task). A step that asks wake:arrive, the engine's own operation, is answered at once and told as the fact it gives ({kind, event_id?, payload}) when the run ends; a step inside a loop or a used workflow waits under its place in the run, so each item is a step of its own. Nothing is kept here and no store or tool is named. A walk that failed ends the run failed, in the engine's words. Its wake a-workflow-was-picked hears the chooser's workflow-chosen facts (a message seed, a matched condition) and a-kept-workflow-is-due the times a noticer tells for kept workflows (kept-workflow-due, a due-time waiter's change_kind); the definition their switch input carries decides which kept workflow, if any, each fact starts. Its wake an-app-asked hears an app's asked-from-an-app fact (a tap on a notice's button, for one); the definition its switch input carries starts only the kept workflows whose own row opts in to that ask, so the next app action is one more row and no list here.

definition.description: The workflow to run (workflow-core: id, name, kind, is_active, version, steps, edges, uses?)

definitions.description: Every definition the run may reach, the first the one it runs

answers.description: Answers so far, by step id

start_at.description: A step to start at: the run walks the part of the workflow reachable from it

run.description: The run's name; left out, the cause that started it

provenance.source: tools/workflows/crates/workflow-component: workflow-core through workflow-engine, built for wasm32-wasip2 by tools/build-engine-modules-for-web-hosts (ENGINE_COMPONENTS)

payload.label: Judge cited code lines against their repositories at the cited commit
payload.job: Check each citation (root/path:line-line@commit) against its repository: the line, or range, holds the quoted text, read at the commit the citation names, or at the root's ref when it names none. One verdict per citation, with the reason when refused.
payload.description: The citation resolver (read-data/citation-resolvers.mjs with citation-resolvers.json) as a tool, so a workflow check can refuse a wrong citation with its reason. Each run is granted ONE repository folder (read-a-folder, from the run's grant): a citation whose root is another repository is answered ok false with 'root not granted to this run'. It reads that folder through git (use-git-in-a-folder), at the commit a citation names or at the root's ref. A repository not here answers ok null, never true. The answer is { result: [{ cite, ok, why, against }] }.

resolver.description: The resolver row to use; code-line for code citations

cite.description: root/path:line or root/path:line-line, with @commit to read at that commit

quote.description: The text the cited line or range has to hold

payload.label: Find the workflows for a job: by words, and by the kinds of moment they wait for
payload.job: Find which of the person's workflows fit a job: rank the shipped workflows and the person's own by the words of the job, and with kinds of moment let the chooser pick by those kinds; each match names the exact input its start takes
payload.description: Give words (the job in a few words) and optionally kinds (the kinds of moment a workflow waits for, from the kinds it names) and own (the person's own workflow rows, each { id, value: { title, job?, steps?, fires_when? } }, read by the caller from wherever the person keeps them). Returns matches (at most eight, each with workflow, label, job, kinds, own, why and next: the input for the start op (wf start: the start op is not built yet)), unknown_kinds (kinds no workflow waits for) and chooser (whether the kinds were answered). Reaches no database and keeps nothing; a find is a read.

words.description: The job in a few words

kinds.description: The kinds of moment to choose by, as the kinds the workflows name

own.description: The person's own workflow rows (id and value), read by the caller

input.words: make short vertical videos from my recorded footage

payload.label: Start a run of one of my workflows
payload.job: Start a run of one of the person's workflows from its recipe: check that the waiter that starts runs is alive on the computer named, then send the start fact with a unique event id
payload.description: Give workflow (the recipe id, as workflow-run-find names it), caller (your AI's record id, such as ai:claude-code-...: the starter, which cancel and answer check), database (the person's database the recipe is in) and input (the run's input object, optional). Answers result {event_id, workflow, database}: keep event_id, it is how show finds the run. Refused before anything is sent when the recipe is not in that database, the engine will not list its wakes, the waiter is not alive, or a field is too big. Runs on the person's own computer through the run's door.

caller.description: Your AI's record id (ai:...), the one that starts the run; cancel checks it against the starter

database.description: The person's database the recipe is in

payload.label: Show where a run of my workflows stands
payload.job: Show where the run started by an event id stands: its waiting-step tasks, grouped by run
payload.description: Give event_id (the one the start answered) and database (the person's database the run's tasks are in). Answers result {event_id, runs: [{run_key, workflow, tasks: [{id, status, step}]}]}. Read only: it writes nothing and shows no task's details.

event_id.description: The event id the start answered

database.description: The person's database the run's tasks are in

payload.label: Stop a run of my workflows for good
payload.job: Stop a run for good: its waiting tasks are withdrawn, so a later answer is refused, and its live step is cancelled on the engine
payload.description: Give run_key (the run's key, from show), caller (your AI's record id: the run's starter) and database (the person's database the run is in), and why (optional). Answers result {run_key, withdrawn: the number of tasks withdrawn, cancelled: whether the run was cancelled on the engine}. Refused, and nothing changed, when the run does not record its starter or caller is not the starter. Runs on the person's own computer through the run's door.

caller.description: Your AI's record id (ai:...), the run's starter

database.description: The person's database the run is in

payload.label: wf: the workflow host on this computer
payload.job: Find, start, answer, show and cancel workflow runs from a chat's shell, on the computer the chat runs on
payload.description: wf is a Rust package of its own (tools/workflow-host), built beside the engine crates it reads by path, never inside them. Its installed binary (tools/workflows/build-wf.sh) answers the chat's wf commands on this computer; the engine does not run it. This row is the list wf's package is kept by: the files in its package_files entry.
